title: Pierogi
subtitle: Polish potato and cheese dumplings
excerpt: Hand-shaped dumplings filled with mashed potato and cheddar, boiled until tender then fried in butter until golden. A comforting staple of Polish home cooking.
sourceNotes: Based on classic Polish ruskie-style pierogi with a potato and cheese filling.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze uncooked on a tray until solid, then transfer to bags. Boil from frozen for 5 to 6 minutes.
recipe.batchNotes: Make a double batch and freeze half before boiling.

content.text: Make the filling first so it has time to cool before you fill the dough.

items.prepNote: finely diced and fried until golden

content.text: Make the filling: mix the mashed potato with the grated cheddar and fried onion. Season with salt. Leave to cool completely.
Make the dough: put the flour in a bowl. Add the eggs and egg yolks and a pinch of salt.
Add 80ml warm water a little at a time, mixing until the dough comes together.
Knead for 5 minutes until smooth. Cover and rest for 20 minutes.
Roll the dough out on a floured surface to 3mm thick. Cut out rounds with a 9cm cutter.
Place a teaspoon of filling in the centre of each round. Fold the dough over to form a half-moon.
Press the edges firmly with a fork to seal. Repeat with the remaining dough and filling.
Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Cook the pierogi in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until they float and are cooked through.
Drain the boiled pierogi. Melt the remaining butter in the frying pan over medium heat.
Fry the pierogi for 2 minutes per side until golden. Serve with soured cream.

items.cause: Edges were not pressed firmly enough.
items.fix: Press with a fork more firmly, wetting the edge with water first.

items.symptom: Dough is tough and hard to roll.
items.fix: Cover and rest for at least 20 minutes before rolling.
